name: Bluetooth scan
plain: Lets the app search for nearby Bluetooth devices.
meaning: Scanning can reveal nearby phones, beacons and wearables and can be used for indoor location. Android 12 split it out of location.

android.permission: BLUETOOTH_SCAN (use neverForLocation flag when location is not derived)
android.prompt_ui: Nearby devices prompt: Allow or Don't allow
android.store_policy: Play: data-safety disclosure for beacon location use

ios.prompt_ui: OK or Don't Allow (one prompt for Bluetooth)
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1; AccessorySetupKit lets apps connect without scan permission (iOS 18)
ios.note: One prompt covers scan, connect and advertise on iOS.

limits.headline: Can search for nearby Bluetooth devices after you tap Allow
limits.user_action: You tap Find devices or Scan nearby
can: Find nearby phones, beacons and wearables
Use scan results to guess indoor position
Scan on iPhone with one prompt that covers scan, connect and advertise
cannot: Scan before you answer the prompt
Use scans for your location on Android 12 and later when the app declares it does not
Scan on Android 11 and older without the location permission
limits.reach_label: Nearby devices, while you use it
limits.differs: Android before 12 needed the location permission to scan; Android 12 and later has a separate Nearby devices prompt.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app search for Bluetooth devices near you.
story.for_you: The app asks to find nearby devices. If you allow it, it can spot your headphones or a new gadget. It can also notice other people's gear in the room.
story.for_makers: Scanning is how an app finds your new device. It also tells the app which beacons and wearables are around, which can be used for indoor location. That is why platforms treat it as sensitive.

use_cases.example: An app finds a new smart bulb and walks you through setup.
A fitness app finds the band you just charged.
A store app picks up shelf beacons and shows deals as you walk by.
A marketing SDK uses beacon scans to learn which stores a person visits.
A mall app uses beacons to give indoor directions.
A local multiplayer game finds other players in the room.
An office app checks that you are close to a door before it opens.

story.android_note: Before Android 12, scanning needed location permission. Android 12 added a Nearby devices option so apps can scan without location.
story.ios_note: One iOS prompt covers scan, connect and advertise.

technical_bounds: Scans can be filtered; location needed if not neverForLocation
iOS prompt is shared across the three roles
Needs foreground scanning in most cases

history.change: BLUETOOTH_SCAN split from location; neverForLocation flag added
Nearby devices permissions split from location
